headline: Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro Close Brazil Campaigns Before Sunday Vote
seoTitle: Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro Close Brazil Campaigns | FMB News
seoDescription: Brazil's leading presidential candidates ended their campaigns before an October 4 vote that polls suggest may require a runoff.
deck: The campaign is over and voting begins Sunday, but no official result exists and a runoff remains only a forecast.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro closed their presidential campaigns on Saturday ahead of Brazil's first-round vote on October 4.

Reuters reported that Lula joined a march through São Paulo, while Bolsonaro took part in a motorcycle caravan in São Paulo state and later rallied in Rio de Janeiro. Both campaigns expressed confidence, although current polling points to a possible runoff rather than a settled first-round result.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Reuters directly reported the final campaign events. Associated Press separately described the election as a highly polarized contest led by Lula and Bolsonaro.
Brazil's Superior Electoral Court says first-round voting runs from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Brasília time on October 4 and will provide official voting updates and results coverage after polls close.

sections.heading: What remains unresolved
paragraphs: No votes had been counted when this article was published. Candidate claims of momentum or a first-round victory are campaign statements, not official findings.
A runoff is required only if no presidential candidate wins more than half of valid votes. Polls suggest that outcome is possible, but the October 25 runoff is not yet certain.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Lula is seeking another term while Bolsonaro is running as the leading conservative challenger and carrying the political legacy of his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.
Brazil's electoral authority has emphasized rules against campaigning at polling places and says official updates will be distributed through its election coverage.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Brazil is a major emerging economy, agricultural exporter and member of BRICS. Its next government can influence global food and commodity markets, climate policy and positions taken by large developing economies. No immediate Philippine policy or price change follows from the campaign events alone.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch official turnout and result bulletins from the Superior Electoral Court, whether either candidate clears the first-round threshold, and any evidence-based reports of voting disruption or disinformation.

verificationNotes: Reuters directly reported the final Lula and Bolsonaro campaign events, while AP independently corroborated the election context.
Brazil's Superior Electoral Court confirms the October 4 voting schedule and is the authoritative source for official results.
Campaign estimates of rally attendance and candidate predictions are not treated as official measures of support.
No official result existed at publication time; the possibility of an October 25 runoff remains a forecast.
The contextual photograph is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is accurately labeled as a 2022 overseas-voting image, not the 2026 campaign or election.
